Heard

Shri Abhishek Pandey, learned counsel for the petitioner, Shri Badrul Hasan, learned A.G.A.
for the State-respondents and perused the impugned F.I.R. as well as material brought on record.

This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner- Sachin Sharma, seeking a writ of certiorari to quash the impugned F.I.R. dated 25.02.2023 registered as F.I.R. No.0103 of 2023, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 406, 504, 506 I.P.C., Police Station Pura Kalander, District Ayodhya.

It has been argued by learned counsel for petitioner that petitioner, himself is the victim of the fraud, as he has also give some amount to co-accused Satendra Singh, who had ensure the appointment of the petitioner in government service.
He further argued that petitioner is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the present case with mala fide intention.
He further argued that out of Rs.4 lakh which was credited in the account of petitioner by the complainant, petitioner has returned Rs.2 lakhs in the complainant account.

The said fact is mentioned in para 8 of the writ Sachin Sharma vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Deptt. Of Home ... on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160665527/
1 petition, hence, the impugned F.I.R. be quashed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned A.G.A., on the other hand, opposed the prayer for quashing of the F.I.R. and submits that the petitioner is named in the F.I.R.

He further submits that as per impugned F.I.R. allegation against the petitioner is that petitioner, who is Manager of Knowledge Park Coaching (Naka),
District Ayodhya along with other co-accused persons, cheated the innocent people by taking their money on the pretext of providing jobs in Government organization.
He further submits that the impugned F.I.R. discloses a cognizable offence against the petitioner, and therefore, the present writ petition is liable to be dismissed.

Having examined the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, perusing the impugned F.I.R., which shows that cognizable offence is made out against the petitioner, we are of the opinion that no interference is called for by this Court in its extraordinary power under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for quashing of the F.I.R. or for grant of any interim relief to the petitioner.
The petition lacks merit and is, accordingly, dismissed.
(Narendra Kumar Johari, J.) (Ramesh Sinha, J.) Order Date :- 22.3.2023
